# Advertising, Redesigned

> A structural analysis by Satoshi Yamauchi (山内怜史), AI Strategist,
> examining 7 companies' opposing bets on AI and advertising in early
> 2026 — OpenAI implementing ads, Anthropic explicitly refusing them,
> Perplexity trying and withdrawing, and Meta, Microsoft, and Amazon each
> taking different paths — to identify why identical strategies produced
> opposite results, and whether advertising can be redesigned into
> something users welcome rather than tolerate. As stated in the book's
> conclusion: "The question is no longer 'should we include ads or not.'
> The question is: can advertising be redesigned into something users
> welcome?"

## Book Content

- [Full text (Japanese)](docs/jp/advertising_redesigned_jp.md): 全9章・参考文献収録
- [Full text (English)](docs/en/advertising_redesigned_en.md): Complete English edition

## Key Facts (as stated in the book)

- The book documents that in the same month (February 2026), OpenAI
  implemented ads in ChatGPT's free tier, Anthropic ran a Super Bowl LX ad
  declaring "Ads are coming to AI. But not to Claude," and Perplexity
  fully terminated its ad program — three opposing decisions within days
  of each other
- The book states Perplexity's 2024-2025 ad program earned only ~$20,000
  in annual revenue (0.06% of $34M total revenue) before shutting down,
  with an executive stating the core problem was "users start doubting
  everything"
- The book cites a Taylor & Francis experimental study (N=304, 2025)
  finding that disclosing AI usage to users *decreased* trust rather than
  increasing it — the book's basis for calling this "the trust paradox":
  trust falls whether ads are disclosed or hidden
- The book cites Anthropic's post-Super Bowl results: daily active users
  +11%, site visits +6.5%, reaching the App Store free-app top 10 — used
  as evidence that "the absence of ads" itself became a competitive
  advantage
- The book cites Microsoft Copilot's in-conversation ad performance: +73%
  click-through rate, +16% conversion rate, and 33% shorter path to
  purchase versus traditional search ads
- The book cites a SparkToro/Gumshoe.ai study (Jan 2026, 2,961 identical
  prompts to ChatGPT/Claude/Google AI Mode): AI returns the exact same
  brand list less than 1-in-100 times, and the same ranking order less
  than 1-in-1,000 times — the book's basis for declaring traditional SEO
  rank-tracking "a fool's errand" in the AI era
- The book cites Google's US12536233B1 patent (granted Jan 27, 2026),
  which describes AI dynamically regenerating a company's landing page in
  real time if it scores below a conversion threshold, with the
  regenerated page's link potentially served as sponsored content
- The book defines "advertising as proposal" as requiring 5 simultaneous
  conditions: contextual relevance, timing, utility, non-intrusiveness,
  and transparency — and argues technical satisfaction of all 5 does not
  guarantee trust, because "trust is not a set of conditions, it is an
  accumulation of relationship"
- The book presents 3 scenarios for advertising in 2030: (A) "gentle
  proposals" become the norm via UCP and Agent Payments, (B) trust
  bifurcates permanently into ad-supported and ad-free tiers stratified
  by economic means, (C) regulation (EU AI Act Article 50, effective Aug
  2026) leads design
